📚 Today you learned

Buy Limit Fill Logic — Why Price-Below-Limit Guarantees a Fill

A buy limit order says "fill me at this price or better (lower)." It executes the moment the market trades at or below your limit — there's no ambiguity, no partial logic, no waiting for a "better" signal. That's the whole mechanism behind today's urgent flag: your GOOG buy limit sits at $365, and the stock has been trading in the $340s. Every session it stayed there, the order was marketable and should have filled — the only real question is exactly which fill price and timestamp, not whether it filled. Compare that to AXTI ($58 limit vs. $77 stock) and SPXC ($200 limit vs. $215+ stock) — both limits sit below the market, so neither is marketable, and both are correctly still resting unfilled. Same order type, opposite outcome, purely a function of where the limit sits relative to price. GTC orders don't expire on their own — they sit live until filled or cancelled, which is exactly how an order placed 11 days ago can execute quietly with nobody watching.

Also today: Marketable order — any order that can execute immediately against the current market price, as opposed to a resting order waiting for price to come to it.
